_cross_item: Strong shared insight across 10 of 13 items: 'k is NOT required to be an integer, so count/aggregate over the integer-valued intermediate (solution, intercept, coordinate, f-value) and map back linearly.' A student who learns it on one item solves B2, B4, B6, B1, B5, B9, B10, A2, A7 the same way. Shared distractor recipes: (a) aggregate of the intermediate instead of k (B1 496 = sum s, B9 153 = sum y); (b) integer-k reading (B4 8, B6 19); (c) off-by-one endpoint adjacent to key (B6 43, B2 12, B5 184/3, B8 93/5, B3 5). The off-by-one recipe puts the key in an adjacent/near pair repeatedly (B2 11/12, B6 42/43, B5 184/3-187/3), which is a cross-item guessing tell.
